218	failure and the file is never truncated or rebuilt. Same-path advances share
219	one lock and the new file is atomically replaced into place; a failed write
220	restores the original bytes. Success returns
221	``{"ok": True, "generation", "tip"}``; failure returns only
222	``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` with category one of
223	``input/auth/integrity/state/io`` and nothing is raised.
224	
225	:func:`reorg_headers` durably checkpoints a verified locator-page batch — a
226	chain reorganization — to the same checkpoint file. The batch is verified
227	with :func:`verify_header_locator_pages` against the caller's ``locators``
228	and pinned ``tip_hash``; the checkpoint at ``path`` must already exist (a
229	missing file is ``io``). The reorg boundary is the closing tip of the last
230	stored step matching the batch's anchor, or the checkpoint's initial anchor
231	when no step matches (a batch anchoring anywhere else is an ``integrity``
232	failure); every step after the boundary is dropped, the new ``locator`` step
233	is appended and ``replaced`` reports the dropped count. The new tip may
234	never drop below the stored tip's height; at the same height a different
235	``block_hash`` — the reorganization itself — is accepted in either status,
236	while the same hash may only move from ``pending`` to ``confirmed``;
237	anything else is an ``integrity`` failure. Re-submitting the exact last
238	locator step (same ``tip_hash``, ``trust``, ``documents`` and ``locators``)
239	is idempotent: it returns the current generation with ``replaced: 0`` and
240	neither bumps the generation nor touches the file. Success returns
241	``{"ok": True, "generation", "tip", "replaced"}`` in that key order; failure
242	returns only ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` with category one of
243	``input`` (bad arguments or locator/batch shape), ``auth`` (signer version
244	or signature), ``integrity`` (boundary, chain, height or same-height
245	conflicts), ``state`` (the existing checkpoint fails its key-order, type,
246	hash or replay checks; it is never truncated or rebuilt) and ``io`` (the
247	checkpoint is missing or cannot be read or written); nothing is raised.
248	
249	:func:`header_locators` derives a fork-location locator request from a
250	checkpoint written by :func:`advance_headers` or :func:`reorg_headers`. The
251	file is strictly
252	reloaded and replayed under the same rules (never rewritten); the replayed
253	history yields the sequence B — the initial anchor and every step's closing
254	tip, ascending, with adjacent equal ``(height, block_hash)`` pairs
255	collapsed — and the request's locators walk B newest-first: up to ten
256	consecutive tail items, then back-steps of 2, 4, 8, ... pinning B[0] at the
257	end, at most 64 items (a 64th item that is not B[0] is replaced by it), in
258	strictly descending height order. ``limit`` must be a plain (non-boolean)
259	integer in 1..500 (default 100). Success returns ``{"ok": True, "tip",
260	"request"}`` in that key order with ``tip`` the stored chain descriptor S
261	and ``request`` the closed ``{"locators", "limit"}`` document (locator key
262	order ``height, block_hash``); failure returns only ``{"ok": False,
263	"error": category}`` with category one of ``input`` (bad path or limit),
264	``io`` (missing or unreadable file) and ``state`` (checkpoint shape, digest
265	or replay mismatch), and nothing is raised.
266	
267	:func:`advance` durably checkpoints a verified batch to ``path``. The
268	checkpoint file is one compact UTF-8 JSON document with the exact declared key
269	order ``generation, anchor, tip, context, state_hash`` and a single trailing
270	newline (non-ASCII written unescaped); ``generation`` starts at 1 and
271	increments per successful advance, ``anchor``/``tip`` are the batch's pinned
272	anchor and closed tip, ``context`` has the exact key order
273	``verified_at, trust, documents, verified_tx_ids`` (the ``now`` at verification,
274	the trust document and the re-verifiable batch verbatim) and ``state_hash`` is
275	the SHA-256 of the canonical (sorted, compact) JSON of the other four fields.
276	The first advance requires a legal ``anchor``; later advances accept ``None``
277	(continue from the stored tip) or the stored tip's ``{height, block_hash}``.
278	Verification itself is :func:`verify_range_exports` unchanged. Same-path
279	advances share one lock and the new file is atomically replaced into place; a
280	failed verification never bumps the generation. An existing checkpoint is
281	strictly reloaded (key order, types, state hash and a context replay at its
282	``verified_at``); any mismatch is a ``state`` failure and the file is never
283	truncated or rebuilt. Failures return only ``{"ok": False, "error":
284	category}`` with category one of
285	``input/auth/expired/integrity/state/io``; success appends the new
286	``generation`` as the final result key.
287	
288	Every successful :func:`advance` also maintains a generation-history sidecar
289	at ``path + ".history"``: one compact UTF-8 JSON document (same serialization
290	rules as the checkpoint) with the exact top-level key order
291	``v, base, records, head``. ``v`` is 1; ``base`` is ``{generation, hash}``
292	naming the generation *before* the first retained record; each record is
293	``{checkpoint, prev, hash}`` where ``checkpoint`` is the persisted five-key
294	checkpoint document, ``prev`` is the previous record's hash (the first
295	record's is ``base.hash``) and ``hash`` is
296	``SHA256(ASCII(prev) || canonical_json(checkpoint))``; ``head`` is the last
297	record's hash. Record generations run consecutively from
298	``base.generation + 1``. A fresh path starts from ``base = {0, Z}`` (Z = 64
299	zeros); a pre-existing generation-``g`` checkpoint without a sidecar is
300	treated as ``base = {g-1, Z}`` with that checkpoint as the first record, and
301	later advances append. Both files are written under the same per-path lock as
302	one transaction: an ``io`` failure restores the original bytes best-effort
303	(a failed compensation surfaces as ``state`` on the next read); crash
304	atomicity across the two files is not guaranteed.
305	
306	:func:`history` reads (and prunes) the sidecar. ``history(path)`` returns
307	``{"ok", "base", "record", "head", "kept"}`` with ``record`` the last
308	generation's record and ``kept`` null; ``generation=`` selects one retained
309	generation (an absent one is a ``state`` failure). ``keep=n`` (mutually
310	exclusive with ``generation``; both must be non-boolean positive integers)
311	retains only the last ``min(n, count)`` records: when nothing is pruned the
312	file's bytes are untouched, otherwise ``base`` becomes the last pruned
313	record's ``{generation, hash}`` and the sidecar is rewritten (the checkpoint
314	file itself never changes). Loading replays every retained generation —
315	shape, state hash, context replay and anchor continuity — so any tampering
316	is a ``state`` failure; a missing or unreadable sidecar is ``io``.
317	
318	:func:`export_history` exports the retained sidecar pages as signed,
319	offline-verifiable page documents. ``export_history(path, key, after=None,
320	limit=50, trust_path=None)`` strictly reloads both the checkpoint and its
321	sidecar under the shared per-path lock and returns one page with the exact key
322	order ``base, records, next, head, checkpoint, auth``: ``base``/``records``
323	are the sidecar's own documents (nested key orders unchanged), ``head`` the
324	sidecar head, ``checkpoint`` the persisted five-key checkpoint (identical to
325	the last retained record's), ``next`` the page's last record generation when
326	another page follows or ``null`` on the final page, and ``auth`` is
327	``{public_key, signature}`` where the Ed25519 signature is made by the 64-hex
328	seed ``key`` over the SHA-256 of the canonical (sorted, compact,
329	unescaped-non-ASCII) JSON of the page with ``auth`` removed. ``after`` is
330	``None`` (start after ``base``) or a non-boolean non-negative integer naming
331	either ``base.generation`` or a non-last retained generation; ``limit`` is a
332	non-boolean integer in 1..200. Bad arguments are ``input``, a missing or
333	unreadable file ``io`` and a corrupt checkpoint/sidecar or unmatched cursor
334	``state``. With ``trust_path`` set to a signer log (see
335	:func:`history_trust`), the log is strictly loaded first (a missing log is
336	``io`` and a corrupt one ``state``) and the page is truncated to the longest
337	prefix, starting at the cursor, whose checkpoints all carry the same key
338	active at their ``verified_at``: it stops just before the first record that
339	would straddle an authorization boundary and sets ``next`` (non-null) so the
340	following page continues there. The seed ``key`` must derive to the public
341	key covering that whole span — an unknown or revoked covering key is an
342	``auth`` failure. A page ending exactly at the retained tail still closes
343	with ``next: null``.
344	
345	:func:`verify_history` verifies an ordered, non-empty list of such pages
346	offline against one pinned 64-hex Ed25519 ``public_key``. Every page must have
347	the exact key order and nested types; ``base``, ``head``, ``checkpoint`` and
348	the signing public key must be identical on every page; each Ed25519 signature
349	must verify over the auth-less canonical page digest. Records must run
350	consecutively from ``base.generation + 1`` and link across page seams through
351	each page's ``next`` (a non-final page's ``next`` is its last record
352	generation), every record hash is recomputed and every checkpoint is replayed
353	(state hash plus the stored batch context) with anchor continuity. The final
354	page alone carries ``next: null``, its last record's hash must equal ``head``
355	and its checkpoint must equal the page checkpoint; missing, duplicate or
356	reordered pages and any tampering are rejected. Success is ``{"ok": True}``;
357	failure is ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` with category one of
358	``input`` (structure/types), ``auth`` (pinned key or signature) and
359	``integrity`` (chaining, pagination or checkpoint replay); nothing is raised.
360	
361	:func:`verify_history_trust` verifies the same pages against a signer
362	rotation/revocation log instead of one pinned page key, so each page's
363	``auth.public_key`` may differ. The ``trust`` document has the exact key
364	order ``root, records, head``: ``root`` is a 64-hex Ed25519 key that must
365	equal the pinned ``root`` argument; every non-empty record has the exact key
366	order ``at, key, status, prev, signature`` with ``at`` a plain
367	(non-boolean) positive strictly-ascending integer, ``key``/``prev`` 64
368	lowercase hex, ``status`` exactly ``active``/``revoked`` and ``signature``
369	128 lowercase hex. The first ``prev`` is 64 zeros, every later one is the
370	previous record's canonical-JSON SHA-256 and ``head`` is the last record's
371	hash; each certificate is the root key's Ed25519 signature over the
372	SHA-256 of the record's canonical JSON with ``signature`` removed. An
373	``active`` record authorizes ``key`` from its ``at`` until the next record;
374	a ``revoked`` one withdraws it until a later ``active``. A page must name
375	the single key active at every checkpoint ``verified_at`` it carries — a
376	page straddling an authorization boundary is rejected — and its signature
377	must verify over the auth-less canonical page digest. All page structure,
378	chaining, pagination and checkpoint-replay rules stay identical to
379	:func:`verify_history`. Failures map to ``input`` (missing/extra/reordered
380	keys, wrong types or hex), ``auth`` (root mismatch, a bad certificate or
381	page signature, an unknown or revoked page key) and ``integrity`` (``at``
382	not ascending, a bad ``prev``/``head``, a boundary crossing, or any
383	record/pagination/checkpoint-replay defect); nothing is raised and success
384	is ``{"ok": True}``.
385	
386	:func:`history_trust` persists such a signer log at its own file path.
387	``history_trust(path)`` strictly loads and returns the ``{root, records,
388	head}`` document; a missing file is an ``io`` failure and any damaged log a
389	``state`` failure. ``history_trust(path, root_seed, at, key, status)``
390	appends one root-signed certificate — the four update fields are all required
391	or all absent — with ``root_seed`` a 64-hex Ed25519 seed (its public key is
392	the log root), ``at`` a non-boolean positive integer, ``key`` a 64-hex public
393	key and ``status`` ``active``/``revoked``. A fresh log must open with
394	``active``; ``at`` must strictly ascend; a ``revoked`` entry must name the
395	currently active key; re-appending the current tail's ``at``/``key``/
396	``status`` is idempotent. A seed whose root does not match the existing log
397	is ``auth``; bad argument shapes are ``input``; read-missing and read/write
398	``io``. The file uses the same compact-UTF-8/unescaped/single-trailing-
399	newline serialization and atomic per-path-locked replace as the checkpoint
400	files, and a failed write restores the original bytes best-effort.
401	"""

451	class _Failure(Exception):
452	    """Internal control-flow exception carrying the public error category."""
453	
454	    def __init__(self, category: str) -> None:
455	        self.category = category
456	        super().__init__(category)

459	def _is_int(value: object) -> bool:
460	    """Plain integer test; booleans are rejected (bool subclasses int)."""
461	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)

464	def canonical_bundle_bytes(bundle: dict) -> bytes:
465	    """Sorted, compact UTF-8 JSON of the bundle with its signature removed.
466	
467	    This is the exact byte document whose SHA-256 the source signs, so signers
468	    and verifiers always agree regardless of incoming key order. The
469	    serialization mirrors :func:`ledger.crypto.canonical_message`: sorted keys,
470	    compact separators, UTF-8 bytes.
471	    """
472	    unsigned = {key: value for key, value in bundle.items() if key != "signature"}
473	    return json.dumps(
474	        unsigned, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")
475	    ).encode("utf-8")
476	
477	
478	def bundle_signing_digest(bundle: dict) -> bytes:
479	    """The 32-byte SHA-256 digest covered by a bundle Ed25519 signature."""
480	    return hashlib.sha256(canonical_bundle_bytes(bundle)).digest()

483	def verify_bundle(bundle: object, trust: object, now: float | None = None) -> dict:
484	    """Verify an offline proof bundle against the local trust document.
485	
486	    Returns ``{"ok": True, "source": ..., "S": ..., "verified_tx_ids": [...]}``
487	    on success — extended bundles also carry ``"verified_accounts"`` — or
488	    ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` on failure. Never raises for
489	    malformed input: every defect maps to one of the five categories.
490	    """
491	    current = time.time() if now is None else now
492	    try:
493	        source, candidate = _validate_inputs(bundle, trust)
494	        _authenticate(bundle, trust, source, current)
495	        blocks_raw = candidate["blocks"] if isinstance(candidate, dict) else candidate
496	        blocks = _recompute_chain(blocks_raw, trust)
497	        descriptor = _tip_descriptor(blocks)
498	        _check_candidate_summary(candidate, descriptor)
499	        _check_response(bundle["response"], descriptor)
500	        has_state = "state_root" in bundle
501	        if has_state:
502	            _check_state_anchor(bundle, blocks)
503	        verified_ids = _verify_proofs(bundle["proofs"], blocks)
504	        verified_accounts = (
505	            _verify_state_proofs(bundle, blocks) if has_state else None
506	        )
507	    except _Failure as failure:
508	        return {"ok": False, "error": failure.category}
509	    except Exception:
510	        # Defensive: structurally unforeseeable inputs must report rather than
511	        # crash the verifying process.
512	        return {"ok": False, "error": ERR_INPUT}
513	    result = {
514	        "ok": True,
515	        "source": source,
516	        "S": descriptor,
517	        "verified_tx_ids": verified_ids,
518	    }
519	    if verified_accounts is not None:
520	        result["verified_accounts"] = verified_accounts
521	    return result

526	
527	def _validate_inputs(bundle: object, trust: object) -> tuple[str, object]:
528	    """Structural validation of bundle and trust.
529	
530	    Returns ``(source, candidate)`` where ``candidate`` is the raw candidate
531	    value (a bare block list or an export-format object carrying ``blocks``).
532	    The bundle itself is never mutated: the signature covers it verbatim.
533	    """
534	    if not isinstance(bundle, dict):
535	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
536	    for field in ("source", "expires_at", "response", "candidate", "proofs"):
537	        if field not in bundle:
538	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
539	    source = bundle["source"]
540	    if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
541	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
542	    if not _is_int(bundle["expires_at"]):
543	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
544	    # The response is itself a JSON object; anything else cannot be checked
545	    # against the recomputed chain descriptor.
546	    if not isinstance(bundle["response"], dict):
547	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
548	    candidate = bundle["candidate"]
549	    blocks_raw = candidate.get("blocks") if isinstance(candidate, dict) else candidate
550	    if not isinstance(blocks_raw, list) or not blocks_raw:
551	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
552	    if not isinstance(bundle["proofs"], list):
553	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
554	    signature = bundle.get("signature")
555	    if signature is not None and (not isinstance(signature, str) or not signature):
556	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
557	    _validate_state_fields(bundle)
558	
559	    if not isinstance(trust, dict):
560	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
561	    if not crypto.is_hex64(trust.get("genesis_hash")):
562	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
563	    sources = trust.get("sources", {})
564	    if not isinstance(sources, dict):
565	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
566	    for name, entry in sources.items():
567	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or not isinstance(entry, dict):
568	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
569	        if not _is_int(entry.get("expires_at")):
570	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
571	        public_key = entry.get("public_key")
572	        # Ed25519 public keys are 32 raw bytes, i.e. 64 hex characters.
573	        if not isinstance(public_key, str) or not _HEX32_RE.fullmatch(public_key):
574	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
575	    allowlist = trust.get("allowlist", {})
576	    if not isinstance(allowlist, dict):
577	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
578	    for name, expires_at in allowlist.items():
579	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or not _is_int(expires_at):
580	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
581	    return source, candidate

584	def _validate_state_fields(bundle: dict) -> None:
585	    """Structural validation of the optional account-state extension.
586	
587	    The four state fields are all-or-nothing; when present, ``state_root`` and
588	    ``state_block_hash`` must be 64-char lowercase hex, ``state_height`` a
589	    non-boolean non-negative integer and ``state_proofs`` a non-empty list.
590	    Every item must carry exactly ``{height, proof}`` and every proof document
591	    exactly the eight documented keys with the right JSON types. Only shape
592	    and type are judged here — domain defects (bad hex, negative balances,
593	    illegal directions) are reported later as integrity/proof failures.
594	    """
595	    present = [field for field in STATE_FIELDS if field in bundle]
596	    if not present:
597	        return
598	    if len(present) != len(STATE_FIELDS):
599	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
600	    if not crypto.is_hex64(bundle["state_root"]):
601	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
602	    if not _is_int(bundle["state_height"]) or bundle["state_height"] < 0:
603	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
604	    if not crypto.is_hex64(bundle["state_block_hash"]):
605	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
606	    state_proofs = bundle["state_proofs"]
607	    if not isinstance(state_proofs, list) or not state_proofs:
608	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
609	    for item in state_proofs:
610	        if not isinstance(item, dict) or set(item) != {"height", "proof"}:
611	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
612	        if not _is_int(item["height"]):
613	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
614	        proof = item["proof"]
615	        if not isinstance(proof, dict) or set(proof) != _STATE_PROOF_KEYS:
616	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
617	        if not isinstance(proof["account"], str) or not proof["account"]:
618	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
619	        if not _is_int(proof["balance"]):
620	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
621	        transactions = proof["confirmed_transactions"]
622	        if not isinstance(transactions, list) or any(
623	            not isinstance(tx_id, str) for tx_id in transactions
624	        ):
625	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
626	        if not _is_int(proof["index"]):
627	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
628	        if not isinstance(proof["state_root"], str):
629	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
630	        if not _is_int(proof["height"]):
631	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
632	        if not isinstance(proof["block_hash"], str):
633	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
634	        if not isinstance(proof["siblings"], list):
635	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)

641	def _authenticate(
642	    bundle: dict, trust: dict, source: str, now: float
643	) -> None:
644	    """Check source trust, every deadline and the optional Ed25519 signature."""
645	    sources = trust.get("sources", {})
646	    allowlist = trust.get("allowlist", {})
647	    source_entry = sources.get(source)
648	    allowlist_expiry = allowlist.get(source)
649	    if source_entry is None and allowlist_expiry is None:
650	        raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
651	
652	    # All deadlines are checked before any signature work: an expired,
653	    # correctly-signed bundle is still unusable. A source listed in both
654	    # ``sources`` and ``allowlist`` is bound by both deadlines.
655	    if bundle["expires_at"] <= now:
656	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
657	    if source_entry is not None and source_entry["expires_at"] <= now:
658	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
659	    if allowlist_expiry is not None and allowlist_expiry <= now:
660	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
661	
662	    public_key = source_entry.get("public_key") if source_entry else None
663	    signature = bundle.get("signature")
664	    if public_key is not None:
665	        # A keyed source must sign: a missing signature cannot authenticate.
666	        if signature is None:
667	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
668	        if not crypto.verify_signature(
669	            public_key, bundle_signing_digest(bundle), signature
670	        ):
671	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
672	        return
673	    # The source reached this point only through the allowlist (every sources
674	    # entry pins a key). An unsigned allowlisted bundle is therefore accepted;
675	    # a signature with no pinned key to check it against is meaningless.
676	    if signature is not None:
677	        raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)

683	def _tip_descriptor(blocks: list[Block]) -> dict:
684	    tip = blocks[-1]

692	
693	def _recompute_chain(candidate_raw: list, trust: dict) -> list[Block]:
694	    """Recompute and validate the whole candidate chain from the pinned genesis.
695	
696	    Mirrors the node's own candidate rules except the endowment balance replay
697	    (an offline client holds no balance convention): genesis anchor, heights,
698	    prev_hash linkage, per-transaction tx_id and Ed25519 signatures, unique
699	    tx_id-sorted transactions, Merkle roots, block hashes and the
700	    pending-only-at-tip rule. Every field is checked on the *raw* JSON value so
701	    coercions such as ``"1"`` or ``1.0`` heights are rejected outright; such
702	    type/domain defects (non-integer or negative height, non-positive or
703	    non-integer amount) are reported as ``input``, while recomputation
704	    mismatches stay ``integrity``.
705	    """
706	    blocks: list[Block] = []
707	    seen_tx_ids: set[str] = set()
708	    for position, block_raw in enumerate(candidate_raw):
709	        if not isinstance(block_raw, dict):
710	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
711	        height = block_raw.get("height")
712	        prev_hash = block_raw.get("prev_hash")
713	        merkle_root = block_raw.get("merkle_root")
714	        block_hash = block_raw.get("block_hash")
715	        status = block_raw.get("status")
716	        txs_raw = block_raw.get("transactions")
717	        # A height of the wrong type or sign is a field-type defect (input),
718	        # not a chain mismatch: strings, floats and booleans must never be
719	        # coerced into plausible integers before the linkage checks below.
720	        if not _is_int(height) or height < 0:
721	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
722	        if not isinstance(prev_hash, str):
723	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
724	        if not crypto.is_hex64(merkle_root) or not crypto.is_hex64(block_hash):
725	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
726	        if status not in ("pending", "confirmed") or not isinstance(txs_raw, list):
727	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
728	        if height != position:
729	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
730	        expected_prev = (
731	            GENESIS_PREV_HASH if position == 0 else blocks[position - 1].block_hash
732	        )
733	        if prev_hash != expected_prev:
734	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
735	        if position == 0:
736	            # Genesis must be the exact block the client pinned: confirmed,
737	            # empty, and carrying the trusted hash (recomputed below too).
738	            if status != STATUS_CONFIRMED or txs_raw:
739	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
740	            if block_hash != trust["genesis_hash"]:
741	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
742	        elif position < len(candidate_raw) - 1 and status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
743	            # A pending block may only sit at the chain tip.
744	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
745	
746	        tx_ids: list[str] = []
747	        for raw_tx in txs_raw:
748	            if not isinstance(raw_tx, dict):
749	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
750	            sender = raw_tx.get("from")
751	            recipient = raw_tx.get("to")
752	            amount = raw_tx.get("amount")
753	            signature = raw_tx.get("signature")
754	            stored_tx_id = raw_tx.get("tx_id")
755	            if not isinstance(sender, str) or not sender:
756	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
757	            if not isinstance(recipient, str) or not recipient:
758	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
759	            # Same rule as the block height: the raw amount must already be a
760	            # non-boolean positive integer — never a coercible string, float
761	            # or bool — so a domain/type defect is reported as input.
762	            if not _is_int(amount) or amount <= 0:
763	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
764	            if not isinstance(signature, str) or not signature:
765	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
766	            message = crypto.canonical_message(sender, recipient, amount)
767	            tx_id = crypto.compute_tx_id(message)
768	            if stored_tx_id != tx_id or not crypto.is_hex64(stored_tx_id):
769	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
770	            if not crypto.verify_signature(sender, message, signature):
771	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
772	            if tx_id in seen_tx_ids:
773	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
774	            seen_tx_ids.add(tx_id)
775	            tx_ids.append(tx_id)
776	        if tx_ids != sorted(tx_ids):
777	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
778	        if crypto.merkle_root(tx_ids) != merkle_root:
779	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
780	        recomputed = compute_block_hash(height, prev_hash, merkle_root)
781	        if recomputed != block_hash:
782	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
783	        # Parsed only after every raw field has checked out; never trusted for
784	        # the comparison decisions above.
785	        try:
786	            blocks.append(Block.from_dict(block_raw))
787	        except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
788	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY) from None
789	    return blocks

850	def _verify_proofs(proofs_raw: list, blocks: list[Block]) -> list[str]:
851	    """Validate uniqueness and cross-block consistency of every proof.
852	
853	    Each entry is ``{"height": int, "proof": doc}`` and the proof document
854	    follows the server shape ``{height, tx_id, index, merkle_root, block_hash,
855	    siblings}``. Proofs for the pending tip are forbidden. The verified
856	    transaction ids are returned sorted ascending.
857	    """
858	    verified: list[str] = []
859	    seen: set[tuple] = set()
860	    for item in proofs_raw:
861	        if not isinstance(item, dict):
862	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
863	        height = item.get("height")
864	        proof = item.get("proof")
865	        if not _is_int(height) or not isinstance(proof, dict):
866	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
867	        if height < 0 or height >= len(blocks):
868	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
869	        block = blocks[height]
870	        if block.height != height:
871	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
872	        # Pending tips never carry trustworthy proofs.
873	        if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
874	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
875	
876	        tx_id = proof.get("tx_id")
877	        index = proof.get("index")
878	        if not crypto.is_hex64(tx_id) or not _is_int(index):
879	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
880	        # The item height and the proof document's own fields must agree with
881	        # the candidate block they claim inclusion in.
882	        if proof.get("height") != height or proof.get("block_hash") != block.block_hash:
883	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
884	        if proof.get("merkle_root") != block.merkle_root:
885	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
886	        if index < 0 or index >= len(block.transactions):
887	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
888	        if block.transactions[index].tx_id != tx_id:
889	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
890	
891	        key = (height, tx_id)
892	        if key in seen:
893	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
894	        seen.add(key)
895	
896	        if not crypto.verify_merkle_proof(
897	            tx_id,
898	            proof.get("siblings"),
899	            block.merkle_root,
900	            block.block_hash,
901	            block.block_hash,
902	        ):
903	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
904	        verified.append(tx_id)
905	    return sorted(verified)

908	def _verify_state_proofs(bundle: dict, blocks: list[Block]) -> list[str]:
909	    """Verify every account-state proof against the bundle's state anchor.
910	
911	    The anchor's confirmed transactions determine the ascending account set;
912	    each proof's ``account`` must belong to it and its ``index`` must be the
913	    account's position in that ordering. ``height`` + ``account`` pairs must
914	    be unique. Every proof is then checked with
915	    :func:`crypto.verify_account_proof` against the bundle's ``state_root``,
916	    ``state_height`` and ``state_block_hash``; any failure — an illegal
917	    direction or hash, a forged leaf, an illegal self-pair, a malformed
918	    sibling path — is a proof failure. Returns the verified accounts sorted
919	    ascending.
920	    """
921	    height = bundle["state_height"]
922	    # The account set of the anchor height: every account touched by a
923	    # confirmed transaction up to and including the anchor block, ascending.
924	    accounts: set[str] = set()
925	    for block in blocks[: height + 1]:
926	        if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
927	            continue
928	        for tx in block.transactions:
929	            accounts.add(tx.sender)
930	            accounts.add(tx.recipient)
931	    position = {account: index for index, account in enumerate(sorted(accounts))}
932	
933	    verified: list[str] = []
934	    seen: set[tuple] = set()
935	    for item in bundle["state_proofs"]:
936	        proof = item["proof"]
937	        account = proof["account"]
938	        expected = position.get(account)
939	        # An account outside the anchor's set, or an index that is not the
940	        # account's ascending position (including out-of-range), is a proof
941	        # failure.
942	        if expected is None or proof["index"] != expected:
943	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
944	        key = (item["height"], account)
945	        if key in seen:
946	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
947	        seen.add(key)
948	        if not crypto.verify_account_proof(
949	            proof,
950	            bundle["state_root"],
951	            height,
952	            bundle["state_block_hash"],
953	        ):
954	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
955	        verified.append(account)
956	    return sorted(verified)

1038	def verify_range_exports(
1039	    documents: object,
1040	    expected_anchor: object,
1041	    trust: object,
1042	    now: int | float | None = None,
1043	) -> dict:
1044	    """Verify an ordered batch of exported range deliveries as one chain.
1045	
1046	    ``documents`` must be a non-empty list of decoded
1047	    ``GET /v1/forks/sync/range/export`` documents (each with the exact key
1048	    order ``source, request_id, mode, expires_at, anchor, blocks, tip,
1049	    attestation``); ``expected_anchor`` is the caller-pinned
1050	    ``{height, block_hash}`` the first page's anchor must strictly equal;
1051	    ``trust`` is the local trust document applied to every page.
1052	
1053	    The pages are re-verified in order: the first page is checked against
1054	    ``expected_anchor``, and every later page's anchor must strictly equal the
1055	    previous page's closed ``tip`` reduced to ``{height, block_hash}`` — which
1056	    also rejects a height jump or a fork at the seam. Transaction ids must be
1057	    unique across the whole batch, not just inside one page, and a pending
1058	    block may only appear on the last page.
1059	
1060	    Returns ``{"ok": True, "anchor", "tip", "pages", "verified_tx_ids"}`` on
1061	    success — ``anchor`` the pinned anchor of the first page, ``tip`` the last
1062	    page's closed tip, ``pages`` the number of pages and
1063	    ``verified_tx_ids`` ascending across every page — or
1064	    ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` on failure with category one of
1065	    ``input/auth/expired/integrity``. Never raises for malformed input.
1066	    """
1067	    current = time.time() if now is None else now
1068	    try:
1069	        if not isinstance(documents, list) or not documents:
1070	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1071	        # The pinned anchor is validated once up front so a malformed caller
1072	        # anchor is an input error even before the first page is inspected.
1073	        anchor = _validate_range_anchor(expected_anchor)
1074	        _validate_range_trust(trust)
1075	        pages = len(documents)
1076	        expected = anchor
1077	        first_anchor: dict | None = None
1078	        last_tip: dict | None = None
1079	        seen_tx_ids: set[str] = set()
1080	        verified_ids: list[str] = []
1081	        for position, document in enumerate(documents):
1082	            # _verify_range_page itself rejects a page whose anchor does not
1083	            # strictly equal ``expected`` — the first page's pinned anchor and
1084	            # every later page's previous tip — so a broken seam or a height
1085	            # jump surfaces as integrity here.
1086	            page_anchor, tip, page_tx_ids = _verify_range_page(
1087	                document, expected, trust, current
1088	            )
1089	            if first_anchor is None:
1090	                first_anchor = page_anchor
1091	            # Transaction ids must be unique across pages, not merely within
1092	            # one re-verified tail.
1093	            duplicates = seen_tx_ids.intersection(page_tx_ids)
1094	            if duplicates:
1095	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1096	            seen_tx_ids.update(page_tx_ids)
1097	            verified_ids.extend(page_tx_ids)
1098	            # A pending block may only sit on the very last page: any block
1099	            # delivered after a pending tip breaks the continuous confirmed
1100	            # chain and cannot be linked to a committed predecessor.
1101	            if tip["status"] == STATUS_PENDING and position != pages - 1:
1102	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1103	            last_tip = tip
1104	            expected = {"height": tip["height"], "block_hash": tip["tip_hash"]}
1105	    except _Failure as failure:
1106	        return {"ok": False, "error": failure.category}
1107	    except Exception:
1108	        # Defensive: structurally unforeseeable inputs must report rather than
1109	        # crash the verifying process.
1110	        return {"ok": False, "error": ERR_INPUT}
1111	    return {
1112	        "ok": True,
1113	        "anchor": first_anchor,
1114	        "tip": last_tip,
1115	        "pages": pages,
1116	        "verified_tx_ids": sorted(verified_ids),
1117	    }

1126	    :func:`verify_range_exports` (a batch chaining each page's tip into the
1127	    next page's expected anchor). Raises :class:`_Failure` with the public
1128	    error category on every defect.
1129	    """

1205

1207	    required here because the caller pins the range anchor directly. The
1208	    optional GET /v1/trust ``source_key_history`` mapping is validated too:
1209	    each source maps to a non-empty ascending array of
1210	    ``{version, public_key, activated_event_id}`` items whose versions are
1211	    dense from 1 with strictly ascending activation ids, both numeric fields
1212	    non-boolean positive integers and the public key 64 lowercase hex.

1218	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)

1221	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)

1223	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)

1225	        # Ed25519 public keys are 32 raw bytes, i.e. 64 hex characters.
1226	        if not isinstance(public_key, str) or not _HEX32_RE.fullmatch(public_key):
1227	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)

1229	    if not isinstance(allowlist, dict):
1230	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1231	    for name, expires_at in allowlist.items():
1232	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or not _is_int(expires_at):
1233	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1234	    history = trust.get("source_key_history")
1235	    if history is not None:
1236	        if not isinstance(history, dict):
1237	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1238	        for name, entries in history.items():
1239	            if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
1240	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1241	            if not isinstance(entries, list) or not entries:
1242	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)

1244	            for position, entry in enumerate(entries):
1245	                if not isinstance(entry, dict) or set(entry) != set(
1246	                    _HISTORY_ENTRY_KEYS

1319	def _recompute_range_tail(anchor: dict, blocks_raw: list) -> list[Block]:
1320	    """Recompute and validate the delivered tail standalone from the anchor.
1321	
1322	    Mirrors the node's own range-tail rules: heights run consecutively from
1323	    ``anchor.height + 1``, the first ``prev_hash`` is the anchor hash and
1324	    later ones link internally, every transaction's tx_id and Ed25519
1325	    signature verifies, tx_ids are unique across the tail and ascending
1326	    inside each block, Merkle roots and block hashes recompute, and a pending
1327	    block may only sit at the tail tip. Every field is checked on the *raw*
1328	    JSON value; type/domain defects (non-integer or negative height,
1329	    non-positive or non-integer amount) are reported as ``input``, while
1330	    recomputation mismatches stay ``integrity``.
1331	    """
1332	    blocks: list[Block] = []
1333	    seen_tx_ids: set[str] = set()
1334	    for position, block_raw in enumerate(blocks_raw):
1335	        if not isinstance(block_raw, dict):
1336	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1337	        height = block_raw.get("height")
1338	        prev_hash = block_raw.get("prev_hash")
1339	        merkle_root = block_raw.get("merkle_root")
1340	        block_hash = block_raw.get("block_hash")
1341	        status = block_raw.get("status")
1342	        txs_raw = block_raw.get("transactions")
1343	        # Same rule as the whole-chain recomputation: a height of the wrong
1344	        # type or sign is a field-type defect (input), never coerced.
1345	        if not _is_int(height) or height < 0:
1346	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1347	        if not isinstance(prev_hash, str):
1348	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1349	        if not crypto.is_hex64(merkle_root) or not crypto.is_hex64(block_hash):
1350	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1351	        if status not in ("pending", "confirmed") or not isinstance(txs_raw, list):
1352	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1353	        if height != anchor["height"] + 1 + position:
1354	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1355	        expected_prev = (
1356	            anchor["block_hash"] if position == 0 else blocks[position - 1].block_hash
1357	        )
1358	        if prev_hash != expected_prev:
1359	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1360	        if position < len(blocks_raw) - 1 and status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
1361	            # A pending block may only sit at the tail tip.
1362	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1363	
1364	        tx_ids: list[str] = []
1365	        for raw_tx in txs_raw:
1366	            if not isinstance(raw_tx, dict):
1367	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1368	            sender = raw_tx.get("from")
1369	            recipient = raw_tx.get("to")
1370	            amount = raw_tx.get("amount")
1371	            signature = raw_tx.get("signature")
1372	            stored_tx_id = raw_tx.get("tx_id")
1373	            if not isinstance(sender, str) or not sender:
1374	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1375	            if not isinstance(recipient, str) or not recipient:
1376	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

1378	            # never a coercible string, float or bool.
1379	            if not _is_int(amount) or amount <= 0:
1380	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)

1382	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

1385	            if stored_tx_id != tx_id or not crypto.is_hex64(stored_tx_id):
1386	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

1388	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

1390	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

1392	            tx_ids.append(tx_id)
1393	        if tx_ids != sorted(tx_ids):
1394	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

1396	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

1401	        # the comparison decisions above.

1404	        except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
1405	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY) from None
